title: Jeremiah Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 16.

questions.question: What instruction did the LORD give Jeremiah concerning marriage?
options: Thou shalt not take thee a wife
Thou shalt marry many wives
Thou shalt take a wife from another land
Thou shalt marry only daughters of priests
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt not take thee a wife
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:2 states that the LORD told Jeremiah not to take a wife.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16, what fate was declared for the sons and daughters born in this place?
options: They shall live long and be prosperous
They shall die of grievous deaths and not be lamented
They shall be priests and kings
They shall be taken captive but protected
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die of grievous deaths and not be lamented
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:4 describes that the sons and daughters born there shall die grievous deaths and shall not be lamented or buried.

questions.question: What were the carcases of the dead described as in Jeremiah 16:4?
options: Meat for the fowls of heaven and beasts of the earth
Buried with great honor
Burned with fire
Taken to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Meat for the fowls of heaven and beasts of the earth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:4 states that the carcases shall be meat for the fowls of heaven and beasts of the earth.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was told to enter the house of mourning to comfort the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:5 instructs not to enter the house of mourning, nor to lament or bemoan them.

questions.question: What had the LORD taken away from the people according to Jeremiah 16:5?
options: Peace, lovingkindness, and mercies
Their land and wealth
Their children and servants
Their ability to speak
questions.correctAnswer: Peace, lovingkindness, and mercies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:5 says the LORD had taken away peace, lovingkindness, and mercies from the people.

questions.question: True or False: Both the great and the small shall be buried and mourned in this land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:6 declares both great and small shall die but shall not be buried nor mourned.

questions.question: Which of the following mourning customs is specifically mentioned as NOT to be done for the dead in Jeremiah 16?
options: Cutting themselves and making themselves bald
Wearing sackcloth
Burning incense
Singing songs
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting themselves and making themselves bald
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:6 says they shall not cut themselves nor make themselves bald for the dead.

questions.question: What are people NOT to do to comfort others over the dead, according to Jeremiah 16:7?
options: Tear themselves in mourning or give the cup of consolation to drink
Gather together for prayer
Offer sacrifices at the temple
Sing hymns of praise
questions.correctAnswer: Tear themselves in mourning or give the cup of consolation to drink
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:7 says men shall neither tear themselves in mourning nor give the cup of consolation for the father or mother.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was told to go into the house of feasting to eat and drink with the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:8 commands Jeremiah not to go into the house of feasting to eat and drink.

questions.question: What will cease in the days of Jeremiah according to Jeremiah 16:9?
options: The voice of mirth, gladness, bridegroom and bride
The sound of the temple bells
The harvest festival
The daily sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of mirth, gladness, bridegroom and bride
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:9 states that the voice of mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride will cease in that place.

questions.question: What question will the people ask Jeremiah after hearing the words of the LORD in Jeremiah 16:10?
options: Wherefore hath the LORD pronounced all this great evil against us?
When will the temple be rebuilt?
Who is our king now?
Why should we give offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore hath the LORD pronounced all this great evil against us?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:10 shows the people questioning why the LORD has pronounced great evil against them.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:11, why did the LORD pronounce judgment on the people?
options: Because their fathers forsook the LORD and served other gods
Because they had no temple
Because they were too few in number
Because they built many altars
questions.correctAnswer: Because their fathers forsook the LORD and served other gods
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:11 states the judgment was because their fathers forsook the LORD and served other gods.

questions.question: What comes first in Jeremiah 16: the command not to take a wife or the declaration that both great and small shall die without burial?
options: Command not to take a wife
Declaration that both great and small shall die without burial
Both occur simultaneously
Neither is mentioned
questions.correctAnswer: Command not to take a wife
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:2 commands not to take a wife before Jeremiah 16:6 declares both great and small shall die without burial.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was told to give the cup of consolation to drink for the dead fathers and mothers.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:7 specifies that men shall not give the cup of consolation to drink for their fathers or mothers.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah instructed not to do regarding sons and daughters in the place he was in?
options: Have sons or daughters
Teach them the law
Send them to the temple
Offer them as sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Have sons or daughters
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:2 instructs Jeremiah not to have sons or daughters in that place.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:8-9, what is Jeremiah instructed not to do, and what will cease in the land?
options: Not enter the house of feasting; the voice of mirth and gladness will cease
Not enter the house of mourning; the voice of lamentation will cease
Not enter the temple; the voice of prayer will cease
Not speak to the people; the voice of prophecy will cease
questions.correctAnswer: Not enter the house of feasting; the voice of mirth and gladness will cease
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:8 forbids entering the house of feasting, and verse 9 explains that the voice of mirth, gladness, the bridegroom, and bride will cease. This connects the prohibition on social joy with the coming sorrow.

questions.question: What question will the people ask Jeremiah after he delivers God's message, as recorded in Jeremiah 16:10?
options: Why has the LORD pronounced great evil against us?
When will the LORD bring us peace?
How can we rebuild the temple?
Who will lead us in battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Why has the LORD pronounced great evil against us?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:10 records the people's question about why the LORD has pronounced such great evil against them, showing their confusion and desire to understand their sin or iniquity.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 16:11, what reason does the LORD give for pronouncing evil upon the people?
options: Because their fathers forsook Him and served other gods
Because they built idols in the temple
Because they refused to fight their enemies
Because they hid the law from their children
questions.correctAnswer: Because their fathers forsook Him and served other gods
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explains that the LORD's judgment is because their fathers forsook Him, walked after other gods, served, and worshipped them, and did not keep His law.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 16:12 describe the people's behavior compared to their fathers?
options: They have done worse and walk after the imagination of their evil hearts
They have repented and turned back to God
They have maintained the same faithfulness
They have forgotten their heritage
questions.correctAnswer: They have done worse and walk after the imagination of their evil hearts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:12 says the people have done worse than their fathers, each walking after the imagination of his evil heart, causing them not to listen to God.

questions.question: What consequence does Jeremiah 16:13 say will happen because of the people's sins?
options: They will be cast out into a land unknown and serve other gods
They will be forgiven and restored to their land
They will receive blessings from the LORD
They will prosper in the land they know
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cast out into a land unknown and serve other gods
questions.explanation: Verse 13 declares that God will cast them out into a land unknown where they and their fathers have not been, and there they will serve other gods, and God will not show them favor.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:14-15, what new phrase will replace the old testimony about the LORD?
options: "The LORD liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north"
"The LORD liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt"
"The LORD liveth, who forgiveth all iniquities"
"The LORD liveth, who heals the brokenhearted"
questions.correctAnswer: "The LORD liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north"
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 say it will no longer be said that the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, but rather that He brought them from the land of the north and all places where He had driven them, promising restoration.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:16 say the LORD will send to gather His people, and what does this imagery teach about God's method?
options: Fishers and hunters to gather them from every mountain and hole
Soldiers to fight for them in battle
Angels to carry them home swiftly
Messengers to proclaim peace
questions.correctAnswer: Fishers and hunters to gather them from every mountain and hole
questions.explanation: Verse 16 uses the metaphor of fishers and hunters sent by God to gather His people from every place, illustrating God's active pursuit and care in restoring them.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:17, how does God view the people's actions and sins?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:17 states that God's eyes are upon all their ways, nothing is hidden from Him including their iniquities, showing His omniscient awareness.

questions.question: Jeremiah 16:18 says God will repay the people's sins. How does He describe this repayment?
options: Recompense their iniquity and sin double
Forgive their sins completely
Ignore their sins
Recompense their sins partially
questions.correctAnswer: Recompense their iniquity and sin double
questions.explanation: Verse 18 clearly states that God will repay their iniquity and sin double because they have defiled His land and filled it with abominable things.

questions.question: What hope or encouragement does Jeremiah express in 16:19 about the Gentiles and the LORD?
options: Gentiles will come to the LORD recognizing the falseness of their fathers' gods
Gentiles will reject the LORD and worship idols
Gentiles will be destroyed for their sins
Gentiles will remain ignorant of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles will come to the LORD recognizing the falseness of their fathers' gods
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:19 portrays the Gentiles coming to God from the ends of the earth, admitting their fathers inherited lies and vanity, showing universal acknowledgment of God's true power.

questions.question: Jeremiah 16:20 asks a rhetorical question about making gods. What is the point of this question?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse asks if a man can make gods unto himself and if they are really gods, emphasizing the futility of idolatry and false gods, teaching trust in the true LORD.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:21 say God will cause the people to know, and what is the purpose of this revelation?
options: God will cause them to know His hand and might, so they know His name is The LORD
God will cause them to forget their sins and be at peace
God will cause them to prosper in the land
God will cause them to fear only other gods
questions.correctAnswer: God will cause them to know His hand and might, so they know His name is The LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 21 promises God will reveal His power and might so that people recognize and acknowledge that His name is The LORD, emphasizing His sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was commanded to take a wife and have children in the land according to Jeremiah 16:2.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:2 explicitly states that he shall not take a wife nor have sons or daughters in that place, demonstrating a prophetic sign of judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 16:5-7 instruct the people to behave towards mourning and consolation, and what does this teach about God's judgment?
options: Do not enter houses of mourning or give consolation, as God has taken away peace and mercy
Mourn openly and give consolation generously to comfort the dead
Celebrate and give thanks even in times of death
Ignore mourning and continue feasting
questions.correctAnswer: Do not enter houses of mourning or give consolation, as God has taken away peace and mercy
questions.explanation: Verses 5-7 command not to join in mourning or consolation because God has removed peace, lovingkindness, and mercies from the people as part of His judgment.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:9 teach about the impact of God's judgment on the daily life and celebrations of the people?
options: The voices of mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride will cease
They will experience abundant joy and celebrations
Only religious festivals will be affected
The people will forget their sorrows quickly
questions.correctAnswer: The voices of mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride will cease
questions.explanation: Verse 9 reveals that God's judgment will cause all joyful sounds associated with life and celebration to stop, highlighting the severity of coming calamity.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 16.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Jeremiah regarding marriage and children in this place?
options: He shall marry and have children
He shall not take a wife or have children
He shall only have daughters
He shall only take a wife
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not take a wife or have children
questions.explanation: The LORD specifically instructed Jeremiah not to take a wife or have sons or daughters in this place, as stated in Jeremiah 16:2.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:4, what will happen to the sons and daughters born in this land?
options: They will prosper
They shall die of grievous deaths
They will be taken captive
They will be blessed in the land
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die of grievous deaths
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that they shall die of grievous deaths and not be buried, indicating a severe fate for those born in that land (Jeremiah 16:4).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 16:5, what does the LORD say He has taken away from His people?
options: Joy and laughter
Peace, lovingkindness, and mercies
Wealth and prosperity
Health and strength
questions.correctAnswer: Peace, lovingkindness, and mercies
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He has taken away His peace, lovingkindness, and mercies from the people (Jeremiah 16:5).

questions.question: What will happen to the great and small in the land according to Jeremiah 16:6?
options: They shall be honored
They shall all die and not be buried
They will be taken to safety
They will receive blessings
questions.correctAnswer: They shall all die and not be buried
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that both the great and the small shall die in this land and shall not be buried, emphasizing the severity of the situation (Jeremiah 16:6).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:10, what will the people ask Jeremiah when he shows them the words of the LORD?
options: Why has the LORD abandoned us?
What is our iniquity?
How can we be saved?
Why must we leave this land?
questions.correctAnswer: What is our iniquity?
questions.explanation: The people will ask Jeremiah what their iniquity is and what sin they have committed against the LORD (Jeremiah 16:10).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:12 indicate about the people's actions compared to their fathers?
options: They have done better
They have done worse
They are the same
They have repented
questions.correctAnswer: They have done worse
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people have done worse than their fathers, walking after the imagination of their evil hearts (Jeremiah 16:12).

questions.question: What will the LORD do according to Jeremiah 16:13?
options: He will bless them with peace
He will cast them out of the land
He will protect them from harm
He will provide for their needs
questions.correctAnswer: He will cast them out of the land
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will cast them out of the land into a place they do not know (Jeremiah 16:13).

questions.question: What new saying will arise according to Jeremiah 16:14?
options: The LORD liveth that created the heavens
The LORD liveth that brought up the children of Israel from Egypt
The LORD liveth that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north
The LORD liveth that provided manna
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD liveth that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the new saying will focus on the deliverance from the land of the north, showing a shift from the past deliverance from Egypt (Jeremiah 16:15).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 16:16, who will the LORD send to gather His people?
options: Shepherds and guardians
Fishers and hunters
Kings and princes
Messengers and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Fishers and hunters
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will send for many fishers and hunters to gather His people (Jeremiah 16:16).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:18, how will the LORD recompense the people's iniquity?
options: With mercy
Double
With blessings
With forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Double
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will recompense their iniquity and sin double, indicating a severe judgment (Jeremiah 16:18).

questions.question: What do the Gentiles admit about their fathers in Jeremiah 16:19?
options: They have inherited lies
They have been faithful
They have great wisdom
They were blessed
questions.correctAnswer: They have inherited lies
questions.explanation: The Gentiles acknowledge that their fathers have inherited lies, vanity, and things of no profit (Jeremiah 16:19).

questions.question: Is it true that Jeremiah 16:20 questions the validity of man-made gods?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:20 questions whether a man can make gods for himself, indicating they are not true gods. This highlights the futility of idolatry.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:21, what will the people come to know?
options: The greatness of their idols
The hand and might of the LORD
The wisdom of their leaders
The futility of their ways
questions.correctAnswer: The hand and might of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people shall know the hand and might of the LORD, emphasizing His power and authority (Jeremiah 16:21).

questions.question: Jeremiah 16:21 reveals what aspect of God's character?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse affirms the sovereignty and might of the LORD, indicating that He will demonstrate His power to the people (Jeremiah 16:21).

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of judgment for idolatry found in Jeremiah 16:20?
options: Colossians 3:5
1 John 5:21
Galatians 5:19-21
Matthew 5:14
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 5:21
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:21 warns against idolatry, echoing the theme of false gods mentioned in Jeremiah 16:20, where the futility of man-made gods is questioned.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:2, what personal restriction did God place on Jeremiah regarding his family life?
options: He shall not take a wife or have children in that place
He shall marry multiple wives but have no children
He shall take a wife but not have sons
He shall have sons and daughters but no wife
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not take a wife or have children in that place
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:2 clearly states that God commanded Jeremiah not to take a wife or have sons or daughters in that place, symbolizing the coming judgment and desolation.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:4 teach about the consequences for those born in the land regarding death and burial?
options: They shall die grievous deaths and not be lamented nor buried
They shall live long but face exile
They shall be mourned but taken into captivity
They shall be buried with great honor
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die grievous deaths and not be lamented nor buried
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:4 reveals the severe judgment: those born in the land will die grievous deaths, not be lamented or buried, and their bodies will become food for birds and beasts, emphasizing divine wrath and desolation.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in Jeremiah 16:5 when God says He has taken away His peace, lovingkindness, and mercies from the people?
options: God's justice and holiness
God's omniscience
God's mercy and grace
God's patience and longsuffering
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and holiness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:5 shows God withdrawing His peace and mercies due to the people's sin, demonstrating His justice and holiness in punishing unrepentant sin, consistent with His righteous nature.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 16:9, what joyous sounds will cease in the land as a result of God's judgment?
options: The voice of mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride
The sound of trumpets and musical instruments
The singing of the Levites in the temple
The shouting of victory in battle
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:9 declares that God will cause the cessation of joyful sounds — mirth, gladness, bridegroom, and bride — indicating a profound communal loss of celebration due to judgment.

questions.question: What reason does God give in Jeremiah 16:11 for pronouncing great evil against the people?
options: Because their fathers forsook God and worshipped other gods
Because they refused to build the temple
Because they did not observe the Sabbath
Because they were oppressed by foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because their fathers forsook God and worshipped other gods
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:11 states that the evil judgment comes because their ancestors abandoned God, walked after other gods, served and worshipped them, showing the root cause as idolatry.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about human sinfulness and divine judgment is conveyed by Jeremiah 16:12 and Jeremiah 16:13?
options: Human sin worsens generational guilt leading to exile without divine favor
Sin can be overcome by human effort and God's favor restored immediately
Only the fathers are guilty, the children are innocent and spared
God is indifferent to sin and does not punish nations
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin worsens generational guilt leading to exile without divine favor
questions.explanation: Verses 16:12 and 16:13 together teach that the people have done worse than their fathers by following their evil hearts, resulting in God casting them out into foreign lands where they will serve other gods and receive no favor, illustrating the doctrine of persistent sin leading to judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 16:14-15 contribute to the biblical narrative of redemption?
options: It prophesies a future restoration from exile, expanding God's saving work beyond Egypt
It denies God's power to save Israel
It focuses only on past deliverance from Egypt
It suggests Israel will never return to the land
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies a future restoration from exile, expanding God's saving work beyond Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:14-15 proclaims a new era when God will bring back Israel not from Egypt but from the north and all lands of exile, illustrating the ongoing redemptive plan and hope beyond initial deliverance.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Jeremiah 16:17 regarding His awareness of human actions?
options: God's omniscience and omnipresence
God's mercy and grace
God's wrath and judgment
God's sovereignty over nature
questions.correctAnswer: God's omniscience and omnipresence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:17 states that God's eyes are upon all their ways and their iniquity is not hidden from Him, illustrating His omniscience and omnipresence in knowing all human behavior.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Jeremiah 16:18, where God promises to recompense iniquity and sin double?
options: The doctrine of divine retributive justice
The doctrine of universal salvation
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of imputed righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine retributive justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:18 teaches that God will repay sin and iniquity double because of defilement of the land, affirming the doctrine of divine retributive justice where punishment corresponds to the severity of sin.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 16:16 and Jeremiah 16:21 together demonstrate God’s sovereignty in judgment and revelation?
options: God sends fishers and hunters to gather His people and reveals His mighty hand
God allows Israel to escape judgment and remain hidden
God’s judgment is limited and His presence unknown
God’s people are victorious without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God sends fishers and hunters to gather His people and reveals His mighty hand
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:16 shows God sending agents to gather the people for judgment, while 16:21 promises that God will cause them to know His hand and might, together affirming divine sovereignty in both executing judgment and making His power known.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's judgment in Jeremiah 16 is unfair because it punishes descendants for their ancestors' sins. How does Jeremiah 16:11-12 address this objection?
options: It shows that the current generation has done worse than their ancestors, justifying judgment
It states that only ancestors are punished, not descendants
It says the descendants will be rewarded despite their ancestors’ sins
It denies that God punishes sin at all
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that the current generation has done worse than their ancestors, justifying judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:11-12 clarifies that the people are judged not merely for ancestral sins but because they have exceeded their fathers in evil, demonstrating that divine judgment is just and based on present guilt.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Jeremiah 16:5-6 and Jeremiah 16:11 convey about God’s response to persistent sin in His covenant people?
options: God withdraws His peace and lovingkindness because of covenant unfaithfulness
God rewards persistent sin with blessing and favor
God ignores covenant breaches and maintains peace regardless
God's response is delayed indefinitely despite sin
questions.correctAnswer: God withdraws His peace and lovingkindness because of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 16:5-6 instruct not to mourn because God has removed peace and mercy; 16:11 links this to covenant unfaithfulness, teaching that persistent sin leads God to withdraw His favor as a just response.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 16:19 reveal about the future inclusion of Gentiles in God’s salvation plan?
options: Gentiles will come to God acknowledging the futility of their ancestors’ false beliefs
Gentiles will be excluded from God’s refuge
Gentiles will continue to worship false gods without repentance
Gentiles will destroy the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles will come to God acknowledging the futility of their ancestors’ false beliefs
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 16:19, God is depicted as strength and refuge, and Gentiles from the ends of the earth will come to Him, recognizing their ancestors' lies and vanity, showing the universal scope of salvation.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 16:20 challenge the common human tendency concerning idolatry?
options: It questions the validity of gods made by human hands, emphasizing their non-divine nature
It encourages making gods to suit personal needs
It claims all gods are equally powerful
It endorses syncretism as a path to God
questions.correctAnswer: It questions the validity of gods made by human hands, emphasizing their non-divine nature
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:20 asks rhetorically if a man can make gods for himself that are truly gods, underscoring that idols fashioned by humans lack divine reality and power, a key polemic against idolatry.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection to the Exodus is made in Jeremiah 16:14-15 regarding Israel’s restoration?
options: God’s future deliverance will be greater, bringing Israel from all lands, not just Egypt
Israel’s restoration will mirror the Exodus exactly with no differences
The Exodus is forgotten and God will not restore Israel
Israel is permanently lost and will never be restored
questions.correctAnswer: God’s future deliverance will be greater, bringing Israel from all lands, not just Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 16:14-15 shifts the redemptive narrative by promising a new deliverance from all lands of exile, expanding on the Exodus theme and portraying God’s ongoing salvation plan.
